You are helping with an AUTHORIZED, READ-ONLY security audit of a Next.js App Router codebase at /opt/nxeon. These files are `"use server"` action modules — every exported async function is a remotely-invokable HTTP endpoint an attacker can POST to directly with arbitrary arguments. DO NOT EDIT ANYTHING. Only Read/grep.

Auth model (from /opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts): `requireUser()` returns current user or throws; `requireAdmin()` throws unless role===ADMIN; `requireStaff()` staff-only; `assertNotImpersonating()` blocks money moves while impersonating. Also `requireGrant(area)`/`requireArea(area)` from lib/staff-grants.ts & lib/rbac.ts gate staff/admin areas. An action is a finding if it (a) has NO guard, (b) uses requireUser for a capability that should be admin/staff (privilege escalation), (c) is IDOR — acts on a caller-supplied id without an ownership/membership check, or (d) moves money/mints credentials/changes roles/settings without the right guard.

For EACH of these files:
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-tokens.ts       (API token minting)
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-staff.ts        (staff accounts / roles / grants)
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-settings.ts     (platform settings)
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-teams.ts        (org/team membership)
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-partner.ts      (partner/agency accounts)
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-agency.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-gift.ts         (gift-code redemption -> wallet)
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-billing.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-payment-method.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-payment-providers.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-payment-fallback.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-dedicated-ip.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-ovh.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-2fa.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-discord-link.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-discord-link-customer.ts

Enumerate every EXPORTED async function and classify. For each report EXACTLY:
- file:line and function name
- the auth guard present (quote the actual line), or NONE
- for functions taking an id/userId/orgId/token: whether ownership/membership is verified (quote the line, or "NO OWNERSHIP CHECK")
- the sensitive capability (mint token, change role, grant staff area, set platform setting, move wallet funds, add payment method, order paid IP, link account)
- VERDICT: OK / IDOR / NO-AUTH / WEAK (under-privileged guard) / PRIV-ESC (customer can gain staff/admin or act on another account)

Quote real lines with numbers. Flag hardest: any function where a CUSTOMER (requireUser) can change their own role or another user's role, grant themselves a staff area, mint a token scoped to another user, redeem a gift code to another account, or set a platform setting. 330	/**
331	 * Persist one section of settings. Bind the section server-side in the panel
332	 * (`saveSettings.bind(null, "general")`) so it's never client-supplied; React's
333	 * useActionState then supplies (prevState, formData).
334	 */
335	export async function saveSettings(
336	  section: string,
337	  _prev: Result | undefined,
338	  formData: FormData,
339	): Promise<Result> {
340	  const fields = SECTION_FIELDS[section];
341	  if (!fields) return { error: "Unknown settings section." };
342	
343	  const area = BILLING_SECTIONS.has(section) ? "billing" : "platform";
344	  const user = await requireArea(area);
345	
346	  const changes: { key: string; value: string }[] = [];
347	
348	  for (const f of fields) {
349	    const raw = formData.get(f.key);
350	
351	    if (f.type === "bool") {
352	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: raw ? "true" : "false" });
353	      continue;
354	    }
355	
356	    if (f.type === "secret") {
357	      const v = (raw ?? "").toString();
358	      if (v.trim() === "") continue; // never clear/overwrite a stored secret with blank
359	      // Encrypt at rest. `smtp_pass` was the last secret in the DB stored as
360	      // plaintext while mailbox passwords and the Cloudflare token both use the
361	      // AES-256-GCM box. Read-back in lib/mailer.ts decrypts, tolerating a legacy
362	      // plaintext row until it is next saved. Never render — SecretField shows
363	      // only `isSet` — so this closes an at-rest exposure, not a live leak.
364	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: encryptSecret(v) });
365	      continue;
366	    }
367	
368	    if (f.type === "enum") {
369	      const s = (raw ?? "").toString().trim();
370	      if (s === "") {
371	        changes.push({ key: f.key, value: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[f.key as keyof typeof SETTINGS_DEFAULTS] ?? "" });
372	        continue;
373	      }
374	      // A <select> constrains the browser, not the request.
375	      if (!f.values?.includes(s)) {
376	        return { error: `“${f.key}” must be one of: ${f.values?.join(", ")}.` };
377	      }
378	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: s });
379	      continue;
380	    }
381	
382	    if (f.type === "int" || f.type === "num") {
383	      const s = (raw ?? "").toString().trim();
384	      if (s === "") {
385	        changes.push({ key: f.key, value: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[f.key as keyof typeof SETTINGS_DEFAULTS] ?? "0" });
386	        continue;
387	      }
388	      const n = Number(s);
389	      if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return { error: `“${f.key}” must be a number.` };
390	      // Refuse rather than clamp, so the stored row always equals what the operator
391	      // can read back off the field. Silent clamping is how a panel ends up showing
392	      // one number while the platform enforces another.
393	      if (f.min !== undefined && n < f.min) {
394	        return { error: `“${f.key}” must be at least ${f.min} (you entered ${s}).` };
395	      }
396	      if (f.max !== undefined && n > f.max) {
397	        return { error: `“${f.key}” must be ${f.max} or less (you entered ${s}).` };
398	      }
399	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: f.type === "int" ? String(Math.round(n)) : String(n) });
400	      continue;
401	    }
402	
403	    if (f.type === "json") {
404	      // Empty clears back to the default (an empty override → the built-in rate
405	      // table). A non-empty value must parse to a JSON object, so the operator is
406	      // TOLD when they fat-finger it rather than the reader silently ignoring it
407	      // (parseRatesOverride fails safe on read, but a silent no-op in the panel is
408	      // exactly the "shows one thing, does another" trap this file avoids).
409	      const s = (raw ?? "").toString().trim();
410	      if (s === "") {
411	        changes.push({ key: f.key, value: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[f.key as keyof typeof SETTINGS_DEFAULTS] ?? "" });
412	        continue;
413	      }
414	      try {
415	        const parsed = JSON.parse(s);
416	        if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object" || Array.isArray(parsed)) {
417	          return { error: `“${f.key}” must be a JSON object, e.g. {"EUR":0.92,"GBP":0.79}.` };
418	        }
419	      } catch {
420	        return { error: `“${f.key}” is not valid JSON.` };
421	      }
422	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: s });
423	      continue;
424	    }
425	
426	    changes.push({ key: f.key, value: (raw ?? "").toString().trim() });
427	  }
428	
429	  // Cross-field: the dunning schedule must run in the order the panel's own hints
430	  // promise — grace (dunning starts) ≤ warn (final-warning email) < terminate (VM
431	  // destroyed). Field-level bounds cannot catch an inverted schedule, and an
432	  // inverted one deletes a customer's server before, or without, warning them.
433	  // worker/billing.ts also clamps on read; this check exists so the operator is
434	  // TOLD, instead of having their numbers silently rewritten behind the panel.
435	  if (section === "billing") {
436	    const day = (k: string) => Number(changes.find((c) => c.key === k)?.value);
437	    const grace = day("dunning_grace_days");
438	    const warn = day("dunning_warn_days");
439	    const terminate = day("dunning_terminate_days");
440	    if (warn < grace) {
441	      return { error: `Dunning warn (${warn}d) cannot come before dunning grace (${grace}d).` };
442	    }
443	    if (terminate <= warn) {
444	      return { error: `Dunning terminate (${terminate}d) must come after the final warning (${warn}d).` };
445	    }
446	  }
447	
448	  // Cross-field: the win-back look-back window must be WIDER than the cooldown, or
449	  // no user is ever both "past the cooldown" and "inside the window" at once and the
450	  // sweep emails no one. Refuse (like the dunning check) so the operator is told,
451	  // instead of the sweep silently falling back to a default they can't see.
452	  if (section === "winback") {
453	    const num = (k: string) => Number(changes.find((c) => c.key === k)?.value);
454	    const delayMinutes = num("deploy_winback_delay_minutes");
